scenes.title: THE SUN VS YOUR WIRES
vo: The Sun can set your wires on fire.
In eighteen fifty-nine, it did, to telegraphs. Could it take out your power?

scenes.title: LEVEL 1
vo: The Sun can hurl billions of tons of magnetized, charged gas at us, arriving in about three days.

scenes.title: LEVEL 2
vo: Earth's magnetic field is our umbrella.
But a storm whose field points south shakes it harder.

scenes.title: LEVEL 3
vo: A shaking magnetic field pushes current through long wires, the same trick a generator uses.
That's how it shocked operators and lit those telegraphs.

scenes.title: LEVEL 4
vo: In nineteen eighty-nine, a smaller storm overloaded transformers.
Quebec's grid failed in ninety seconds, leaving six million people in the dark.

scenes.title: THE ANSWER
vo: But in twenty twelve, a storm that strong missed us by about a week.

scenes.title: IF IT HITS
vo: Today it would scramble GPS and radio, and could cut power for weeks.
But in eighteen fifty-nine, the aurora was bright enough to read a newspaper by.
